claims.topic: Safari Web Extension availability and packaging model on iPadOS
claims.final_claim: Safari web extensions work in Safari on iOS/iPadOS 15 and later. Each extension ships as an iOS app extension inside a containing app. Distribution requires the Apple Developer Program. Testing on a device, TestFlight and the App Store all require a signed extension and a signed containing iOS app. The simulator is the only unsigned option.

claims.final_claim: App Store Connect has a web-based Safari Web Extension Packager. It turns uploaded extension resources (manifest plus files) into a signed app and extension for iOS/iPadOS/macOS, from any browser and without a Mac or Xcode. Builds then go through TestFlight or the App Store. Packaging time counts against the 25 Xcode Cloud hours per month included with the membership. It was introduced with Safari 26.

claims.topic: User enablement and per-site permission on iPad
claims.final_claim: The user turns the extension on in Safari (search field > Manage Extensions) or in Settings > Apps > Safari > Extensions, and can switch it on or off for an individual website. Site access is granted per website (Ask/Allow/Deny). Content scripts do not run in a tab until the user grants access through the extension's access alert. The activeTab permission grants access without a prompt, but only for the current site in the current tab after the user explicitly invokes the extension, and it is revoked when the tab navigates to another site. In Safari 17+, a site grant applies across all profiles and Private Browsing.

claims.topic: Reported iOS background/service-worker termination bug
claims.final_claim: Developers report that since iOS 17.4 the extension service worker or background can be killed permanently about 30-45 s after install and then no longer wakes for sendMessage or webNavigation. An Apple Frameworks Engineer said it was fixed in 17.6.1. Developers later said it still happened on 18.x (last report Aug/Sep 2025). The reported workaround is background.scripts with persistent:false instead of service_worker. Behavior on iPadOS 27 is unverified.

claims.topic: Native messaging direction and limits on iOS
claims.final_claim: Only background scripts and extension pages can call browser.runtime.sendNativeMessage. Content scripts cannot. The manifest needs the 'nativeMessaging' permission. Safari ignores the application id and delivers the message to the containing app's native app extension, which handles it in beginRequest(with:) and replies through completeRequest. On iOS, the containing app cannot send messages to the extension's JS. connectNative with SFSafariApplication.dispatchMessage is documented only for a macOS containing app, and SFSafariApplication exists only on macOS (10.12+).

Pointer and touch coordinates are fractional since Safari 26.2. The WebKit Touch.touchType ('stylus' or 'direct') is available since iOS 10.

claims.topic: Routing Pencil to overlay while finger keeps scrolling; known web limitations
claims.final_claim: CSS touch-action applies to all direct-manipulation pointers, pen as well as touch (W3C Pointer Events 3, Recommendation 30 June 2026). A page-wide touch-action:none overlay would therefore also block finger panning, and pen-only capture has to be decided per pointer in JS. CSS pointer-events cannot tell pen from finger. An overlay with pointer-events:none receives no events from either, so it cannot be 'pointer-events:none for fingers' only. Candidate approach (inferred, untested): non-passive capture-phase touchstart/touchmove listeners at document level that call preventDefault only when Touch.touchType==='stylus', with ink drawn in a non-interactive layer. Or toggle the overlay's hit-testing on pen hover/pointerdown, which is racy. Developer forum reports with no Apple reply say Safari/WKWebView drops simultaneous finger input while the Pencil is down (FB16411500; the W3C spec lets UAs do this for palm rejection) and that Pencil Pro pointermove looks coarser than touchmove.
claims.verifier_note: W3C quotes and the 'W3C Recommendation 30 June 2026' status are verified. Forum threads 773213 (Jan 2025; the OP filed FB16411500; no Apple reply) and 776468 (Mar 2025; 0 replies) are confirmed. Their source kind should be 'forum (developer report, no Apple reply)', not 'apple_forum_dts'. The researcher's mechanism, 'keep the overlay pointer-events:none for fingers', does not work as written. Relevant Safari 27 fixes: touch event property values sometimes swapped (171567543); preventDefault() in pointerdown now suppresses mousedown/mouseup on iOS (174864309). Test on 27.0.
claims.evidence_excerpt: W3C: "The touch-action CSS property determines whether direct manipulation interactions (which are not limited to touch, despite the property's name) MAY trigger the user agent's panning and zooming behavior." / "devices that support both touch and pen interactions may ignore touch inputs while the pen is actively being used ... Currently, it is not possible for authors to suppress this behavior." / forum: "Apple Pencil down blocks touch input until lifted"

claims.topic: Pencil hover and Pencil Pro gestures in web content
claims.final_claim: WebKit (Safari 16.1) says Apple Pencil hover shows hover states in web browsers. Apple's Pencil Pro tech specs list hover for iPad Pro (M4 and M5), iPad Pro 11-inch (4th gen), iPad Pro 12.9-inch (6th gen), iPad Air (M2 and M3) and iPad mini (A17 Pro). The iPad User Guide hover page also covers iPad Air M4. No official source says which DOM events web pages get during hover. No web API is documented for Pencil Pro squeeze or double-tap. Natively these are UIPencilInteraction (squeeze: UIPencilInteraction.Squeeze, iPadOS 17.5+). Barrel roll is exposed natively as UITouch.rollAngle (iPadOS 17.5+), not through UIPencilInteraction. PointerEvent.twist is exposed in Safari (BCD: Safari 13+, iOS mirrors), but no source says whether it reports Pencil Pro barrel roll; that needs a device test.

The researcher's T4 and environment list include Air M4, which a support.apple.com iPad guide hover page appears to support (seen in search results only, not fetched). The original text wrongly grouped barrel roll under UIPencilInteraction, and it missed PointerEvent.twist as a candidate web signal to test.

verifier_added.topic: Extension-to-backend fetch needs granted per-site access (CORS)
verifier_added.claim: Since Safari 18.4, CORS for Web Extension pages (including background) respects the per-site permissions the user granted. Apple says developers must call browser.permissions.request({origins: [...]}) before any fetch() that CORS would block. Safari 27 separately fixed cross-origin XMLHttpRequest triggering an extra permission request. So the extension's calls to our backend depend on the user granting the backend origin, unless the backend's CORS headers allow the extension origin.

device_tests_proposed: T1 Enablement: Install the TestFlight build on the user's iPad (record the model and iPadOS 27.x). Turn the extension on through Safari > Manage Extensions. Expected: the containing app's SFSafariExtensionManager.stateOfExtension.isEnabled flips to true, and SFSafariSettings.openExtensionsSettings opens the extension's settings page (iPadOS 26.2+).

T2 Per-site/iframe permissions: Open a bCourses page with an embedded Kaltura video. Record which permission alerts appear (bcourses domain vs Kaltura KAF/CDN domains), and whether the all_frames content script loads in each iframe (log location.origin from every frame to the backend). Expected: the script runs in the top frame after grant; iframe behavior is unknown.

T3 Pencil vs finger: On the overlay, log pointerType, pressure, tiltX/Y, altitudeAngle, getCoalescedEvents length and touchType for Pencil Pro and for a finger. Expected: 'pen' vs 'touch'. Check that finger scrolling of the Canvas page still works while Pencil mode is armed, and whether a finger touch during an active Pencil stroke is dropped (forum reports say yes).

T4 Hover: On a hover-capable iPad (Air M2/M3/M4, Pro M4/M5), hold the Pencil above the overlay and log pointerover/pointermove with buttons==0. Expected: unknown; record whether pen hover events fire.

T5 Scribble: With Scribble on (Settings > Apple Pencil), draw circles and words on the overlay near Canvas text inputs. Expected: no text insertion on the non-editable overlay and no lost pointerdown events (WebKit 217430 fixed).

T6 Fullscreen: Tap fullscreen on Berkeley's Kaltura player in Safari. Record whether it becomes native AVKit fullscreen (the overlay disappears) or element fullscreen (document.fullscreenElement is set inside the iframe), and whether an overlay injected inside the iframe stays visible. Repeat for a YouTube embed.

T7 captureVisibleTab: With a video playing and then paused, and the Safari toolbar both expanded and collapsed, capture from the background. Check that the video pixels are not black, measure the vertical offset between the selection rectangle and the image (cropping bug), and measure latency. Repeat with Split View and Stage Manager window sizes.

T8 Background lifecycle: Leave the extension idle for 1, 5 and 30 minutes, switch to Notability and back, then make a Pencil selection. Expected: runtime.sendMessage wakes the background and the selection reaches the backend. Run the non-persistent 'scripts' and service_worker variants on iPadOS 27.

T9 Native messaging: Run sendNativeMessage round trips with payloads of 1 KB, 100 KB and 1 MB, 5 MB. Record latency, failures and appex memory in Console. Try runtime.connectNative on iOS and record whether a port opens and how long it lives.

T10 Home Screen web app: Add bCourses to the Home Screen with 'Open as Web App' on, and then again with it off. Record whether the content script runs in each. Expected (unverified): not in the web app, yes in the Safari tab.

T11 Canvas Student app: Open the same course video in the Canvas Student app. Confirm the extension does not run there. Turn on 'Open external tools in Safari' and confirm the Kaltura tool opens in Safari with the extension active.

T12 Lifecycle honesty (A14): While a session is active, switch from Safari to Notability and back, close the Safari tab, and force-quit Safari. Record which extension and backend events fire, so that session state never infers 'ended' from a missing heartbeat alone.

T13 WKWebExtension fallback (F1): In the app's own WKWebView with the same extension loaded, log in to bCourses through CalNet/Duo, play Kaltura video in-page, and repeat T3, T6 and T7 there, using WKWebView.takeSnapshot instead of captureVisibleTab.

claims.topic: PKCanvasView as a transparent overlay over WKWebView
claims.final_claim: Apple documents drawing over other content by making PKCanvasView non-opaque with a clear background (WWDC19). PKCanvasView is a scroll view. With finger drawing disabled, WWDC19 says "only Pencil will draw and one finger will scroll" (on the canvas). The hitTest docs say a view is hit even where its content is transparent. A full-screen transparent PKCanvasView over WKWebView is therefore expected to take finger pans and taps meant for the page (inferred). UIKit's documented generic pass-through, overriding hitTest(_:with:) or point(inside:with:) ("you might override it to hide touch events from subviews"), works per point, not per touch type. No documented API passes only finger touches through while keeping Pencil touches. isDrawingEnabled (18.0+) turns drawing off, but its effect on touch routing is not documented. PKCanvasView.drawingGestureRecognizer (13.0+) is exposed so apps can "set up gesture recognizer exclusions or failure requirements".
claims.verifier_note: The quoted doc sentence reads "The canvas view handles all of the touch events and data coming from Apple Pencil". It is about Pencil input, not a statement that the canvas takes every touch. 'No Apple API passes finger touches through' overstates things: generic hitTest/point(inside:) pass-through is documented, just not by touch type. The conclusion (inferred, needs a device test) still holds.

claims.topic: Documented primitives for pencil/finger routing
claims.final_claim: UIKit exposes the pieces needed to separate Pencil from finger in our own view hierarchy. UITouch.type == .pencil identifies Apple Pencil. UIGestureRecognizer.allowedTouchTypes (default: all types) can limit a recognizer to Pencil only. When cancelsTouchesInView is true (the default), a recognized gesture's touches are withheld from the view and earlier ones are cancelled. UIScrollView.panGestureRecognizer is exposed so apps can control which pans the scroll view recognizes. Together this suggests: a pencil-only recognizer on the web view's container, plus limiting the web view's scroll pan to .direct touches.

Community forum posts (not Apple) report that event.allTouches is empty during hitTest and that mixing a Pencil touch with a finger touch ends the Pencil touch. A DTS engineer said UIHostingController's hitTest implementation 'is also not guaranteed'.

claims.topic: Angles, barrel roll and hover

UIHoverGestureRecognizer.zOffset (iPadOS 16.1+) is 1 at maximum distance, approaches 0 as the Pencil gets closer, and is 0 on devices without support. claims.topic: UIPencilInteraction double tap / squeeze and user preferences
claims.final_claim: UIPencilInteraction (iPadOS 12.1+) reports double taps through pencilInteraction(_:didReceiveTap:) (17.5+), which replaces the deprecated pencilInteractionDidTap(_:). It reports squeezes through pencilInteraction(_:didReceiveSqueeze:) (17.5+); "Only Apple Pencil Pro supports squeeze interactions." Squeeze has began/changed/ended/cancelled phases. UIPencilInteraction.preferredTapAction (12.1+) and preferredSqueezeAction (17.5+) are read-only class properties holding the user's choice from Settings > Apple Pencil > Actions, and apps are told to respect .ignore. If the preferred squeeze action is to run a system shortcut, the app is not sent the squeeze event (WWDC24). UIPencilHoverPose (17.5+) gives location, zOffset, azimuth, altitude and roll. Squeeze.hoverPose is optional and is nil "if Apple Pencil isn't close enough to the screen to detect a hover, or if the device doesn't support hover." isEnabled (default true) turns reporting on or off.

claims.final_claim: By default Scribble works in any editable UITextInput, including editable web content in WebKit. To stop nearby text fields from taking Pencil input, return false from UIScribbleInteractionDelegate.scribbleInteraction(_:shouldBeginAt:) while in drawing mode. UIIndirectScribbleInteraction is for UI that becomes editable after a tap. Apple does not document whether a UIScribbleInteraction attached to our WKWebView suppresses Scribble inside web-page text fields. A community forum post (not Apple) reports that disabling Scribble made Pencil pointerdown events fire consistently in Safari.

claims.topic: Alternative: capture Pencil inside our WKWebView via web Pointer Events
claims.final_claim: WebKit has supported Pointer Events, including stylus input, since Safari 13 (WebKit blog, Dec 20, 2019). Since Safari 18.2 (iOS/iPadOS 18.2, WebKit blog Dec 9, 2024), WebKit also supports PointerEvent.getCoalescedEvents() and getPredictedEvents(), and altitudeAngle/azimuthAngle "to easily determine the angle between Apple Pencil and the X-Y or Y-Z planes of the screen." The 2021-2023 community reports that getCoalescedEvents was unsupported are therefore out of date. JavaScript injected into our own WKWebView could handle pen pointers while leaving touch pointers to the page. claims.topic: SwiftData local persistence semantics
claims.final_claim: SwiftData (iPadOS 17+) stores models locally. @Attribute(.externalStorage) keeps binary values, such as PKDrawing data, next to the store rather than inside it. ModelContext changes stay in memory until an implicit save or an explicit save(). The main context autosaves after changes and 'at various times during the lifecycle of windows, scenes, views, and sheets', without saying exactly when. Apple publishes no write-latency figures.

SwiftData automatically sets this property to true for the model container's mainContext."

claims.topic: File protection, atomic writes, termination callbacks

For apps that support background execution, applicationWillTerminate is 'generally not called when the user quits the app', and when it does run it has about 5 seconds.

claims.topic: System 'circle with Apple Pencil' in iPadOS 27 (not an app API)
claims.final_claim: iPadOS 27 brings Visual Intelligence to iPad: "Ask Siri AI about virtually anything on your display with a screenshot. Just tap the item with your finger or circle it with Apple Pencil to find out more." It is a system feature, and no public API lets a third-party app receive the circle gesture itself or run its own global overlay. However, the Visual Intelligence framework (iOS/iPadOS 26.0+) is a documented, user-initiated and system-mediated way for a participating app to receive the captured content. "When a person performs visual search on the visual intelligence camera or a screenshot, the system forwards the information captured to an App Intents query you implement." The app's IntentValueQuery receives a SemanticContentDescriptor with en_US labels and a pixelBuffer ("The pixel buffer that visual intelligence captures"), and it returns results that appear in the system UI and can open the app. WWDC26 says that on iPad "the primary entry point is screenshots." Undocumented: whether pixelBuffer is the circled region or the whole screenshot, and whether it works over DRM video. Availability: Apple Intelligence-capable iPads (iPad mini A17 Pro, M1 and later) with the device language set to a supported English variant. Siri AI is in beta, English first, and not initially available in the EU on iPadOS.
claims.verifier_note: 'No public API sends that selection into a third-party app' is too strong. The documented VisualIntelligence plus App Intents path delivers the screenshot pixel buffer and labels to an opted-in app. This bears directly on G2: a user could circle content in the Canvas Student app or Safari and pick our app's results, without any overlay. It is not silent and it is not our UI, so it only partly meets R01/R06. apple.com/os/ipados is a marketing page and should be labelled apple_marketing, not apple_doc.

device_tests_proposed: T1 Model check: on the user's iPad open Settings > General > About > Model Number. Expect A3266/A3267/A3270/A3268/A3269/A3271 (Air M3), A3357 to A3362 (Pro M5), or A3459-A3464 (Air M4) / A2993/A2995/A2996 (mini A17 Pro) if bought in 2025. Confirm the Pencil Pro pairs. If the result is A3354-A3356 (iPad A16), Pencil Pro is impossible, so re-scope.

T2 Naive overlay baseline: put a full-screen transparent PKCanvasView (.pencilOnly) over WKWebView showing a bCourses page. With one finger, swipe and tap a link. Expected (inferred): the canvas takes the touch and the page does not scroll or follow the link. This establishes that custom routing is needed.

T3 Pencil-only recognizer routing: remove the canvas, add a UIPanGestureRecognizer with allowedTouchTypes = [.pencil] and cancelsTouchesInView = true to the WKWebView container, and set webView.scrollView.panGestureRecognizer.allowedTouchTypes = [.direct]. Check: finger scroll, pinch, link taps and video play/scrub/fullscreen/captions all work. A Pencil stroke across a link and across the video player neither navigates, scrolls nor toggles playback, and the ink is continuous. Log page JS pointerdown/touchstart to see whether the page receives a Pencil event before cancellation. Repeat on iPadOS 27.

T4 Mixed touches (A26): write with Pencil while resting a palm or finger, and while scrolling with a finger. The stroke must not end early (a community report says mixed touch types end the first touch). The finger scroll must still move the page, and ink anchors must move with the page content.

T5 A03 false triggers: normal scroll, tap, write and scrub for 5 minutes in Write mode. Expect zero ask/explain triggers. Then enter Ask mode, circle a formula, and confirm the app returns to normal operation afterwards.

T6 Scribble: in Write and Ask modes, write with Pencil over a bCourses search box or discussion editor. Without suppression, expect Scribble to insert text. With a UIScribbleInteraction delegate returning false (or focus blocking), expect no text insertion. Record whether suppression works inside WKWebView.

T7 Pencil Pro signals: log UITouch.rollAngle (Pencil Pro non-zero while rotating; expected 0 with a USB-C Pencil), hover zOffset from 0 to 1 (within about 12 mm), didReceiveSqueeze phases, preferredSqueezeAction and preferredTapAction after changing Settings > Apple Pencil > Actions, and UIPencilHoverPose.location during a squeeze. Confirm squeeze never fires with a non-Pro Pencil.

T8 Default policy semantics: with drawingPolicy = .default, toggle the system 'Only Draw with Apple Pencil' / 'Draw with Finger' setting and show or hide the PKToolPicker. Expected: the picker visible means the setting is respected; the picker hidden means only Pencil draws.

T9 Persistence and force-quit (A27): draw 200 strokes, force-quit from the app switcher within 1 s of the last stroke, go offline, relaunch. Expect every stroke up to the last debounced save to be restored as editable ink, the AI additions layer present and independently deletable, and no duplicate versions. Measure dataRepresentation() plus atomic write time at 1k, 5k and 20k strokes, and SwiftData save() latency.

T10 Content version: draw with Reed Pen on iPadOS 27 and check requiredContentVersion (expected version4 or higher). Set maximumSupportedContentVersion = .version3 on the canvas and tool picker and confirm the reed and newer inks are unavailable. Open the note on an iPhone on an older OS and confirm the thumbnail fallback appears.

T11 Export fidelity: render PKDrawing into a PDF context with draw(in:frame:from:darkUserInterfaceStyle:) (26+) and image(from:scale:). Check whether the PDF output is vector or raster before promising Notability or OneNote quality.

T12 System gesture coexistence: in our app with the pencil recognizer active, run the Pencil corner-swipe (screenshot/Quick Note) and iPadOS 27 Visual Intelligence circle. Confirm our recognizer does not block them and they do not create stray strokes.

T13 File protection: with notes written using default protection vs .completeFileProtection, lock the device during a background audio session and trigger a save. Expected: .complete writes fail while locked; the default succeeds after first unlock.

It declares UIBackgroundModes 'screen-capture' ('so the stream survives backgrounding for full-display capture') and 'audio' (so the microphone tap keeps producing samples), and it activates an AVAudioSession in playAndRecord before a full-display capture. T2 Course audio via .audio: with capturesAudio = true, play (a) a bCourses/Kaltura video in Safari, (b) the same video in the Canvas Student app, (c) the Music app as a control. Measure the RMS of the .audio buffers. Expected: non-zero audio for the Music control; record whether (a) and (b) are non-zero or all zeros.

T3 DRM/black-frame check: during T2, inspect .screen frames of the video area. Expected for FairPlay content: a black video region. Also record whether Safari or Canvas pause playback when capture starts (sceneCaptureState/isCaptured reactions).

T4 Mic separation: enable the mic in the picker, speak while the course plays on speaker, then on AirPods. Expected: the user's voice in .microphone. Measure how much course audio leaks into .microphone on speaker vs AirPods, and confirm .audio carries no mic signal.

T5 mixWithOthers: activate .playAndRecord with and without .mixWithOthers while a Safari video plays. Expected: without it, Safari playback is interrupted; with it, playback continues. Also test setVoiceProcessingEnabled(true) for ducking of the course audio.

T6 Stop paths: stop from the system recording indicator or Control Center, lock the screen, start a phone or FaceTime call, and trigger low memory. Expected: stream(_:didStopWithError:) with userStopped or systemStoppedStream. Log the codes and check whether any restart is possible without showing the picker again (expected: no).

T7 Force-quit: swipe our app away during capture. Expected: in-process ScreenCaptureKit capture ends and the indicator disappears. For the F1 broadcast extension, record whether the broadcast continues after the host app is force-quit.
T8 Picker options: on iPadOS 27, record exactly what the SCContentSharingPicker offers (entire screen, this app, another single app?) and which indicator is shown while capturing.
T9 excludesCurrentProcessAudio: play a 1 kHz tone from our app while capturing on 27.0 and on 27.2 or later. Expected: 0 dB suppression on 27.0 (forum report); the tone suppressed on 27.2 or later.

T10 Frame rate/memory: measure delivered fps and our process memory at full resolution vs 1/4 resolution on the user's actual iPad model. Repeat for the F1 extension and watch for EXC_RESOURCE crashes at about 50 MB.
T11 iPhone parity: repeat T1, T2 and T6 on the user's iPhone with iOS 27 to confirm independent per-device start and stop.

claims.topic: Default suspension when the user switches to Safari or Canvas
claims.final_claim: Leaving the app for Safari or Canvas Student moves our scene to the background. It does not disconnect the scene or end the process. Unless a legitimate background mode or task is active, iOS/iPadOS suspends the app shortly afterwards and no code runs. So switching apps is not an end event and gives no reliable chance to do ongoing work.

claims.topic: UIApplication background task (short finish window)
claims.final_claim: beginBackgroundTask(withName:expirationHandler:) only asks for a limited extra amount of time to finish work. Every call must be balanced by endBackgroundTask, or the system kills the app. DTS says to expect about 30 seconds and not to depend on the exact number. App extensions use ProcessInfo.performExpiringActivity instead.

claims.topic: Audio background mode for mic recording
claims.final_claim: With UIBackgroundModes 'audio' and an active playAndRecord session (record also works but must not be used here), microphone recording continues after the app goes to the background, including when the screen locks. The .record category 'has the effect of silencing virtually all output on the system' and cannot take mixWithOthers (that option is only allowed for playAndRecord, playback and multiRoute), so it would mute the course video in Safari or Canvas. Use playAndRecord + mixWithOthers. AVAudioSession.ErrorCode.cannotStartRecording (iOS/iPadOS 13.0+) 'usually occurs when an app starts a mixable recording from the background and it isn't configured as an Inter-App Audio app'. The rule that the mic must be started in the foreground is an inference from that sentence. Documented: since iOS 10 the system deactivates an app's audio session when it suspends the app. If the mic stops (interruption, user toggle), the audio mode no longer keeps the process alive and the app will be suspended.
claims.verifier_note: The cited quotes are accurate. However, the claim treats record and playAndRecord as interchangeable, and they are not: record silences system output, which would break course-audio playback, and the product needs that audio. The playAndRecord excerpt the researcher relied on is about continuing to *play* audio in the background; background *recording* is stated on the record page. claims.topic: Force-quit from the app switcher
claims.final_claim: When the user force-quits by swiping up in the app switcher, iOS terminates the app if it is running and sets a flag that blocks background launches until the user next opens the app manually (DTS 685525). Background URLSession transfers are cancelled and the app is not relaunched automatically (URLSessionConfiguration.background doc). applicationWillTerminate(_:) (iOS/iPadOS 2.0+, not deprecated) has about five seconds to run. For apps that support background execution it is 'generally not called when the user quits the app because the app simply moves to the background in that case'. Here 'quits' means leaving the app, not an app-switcher force-quit. The doc says it 'may be called in situations where the app is running in the background (not suspended) and the system needs to terminate it'. Apple does not document whether it fires on a user force-quit of an app that is running in the background, for example while capturing. That needs a device test.

claims.topic: iPadOS 27 ScreenCaptureKit: in-process capture with the screen-capture background mode
claims.final_claim: ScreenCaptureKit is available on iOS/iPadOS 27.0+ and its overview states 'ScreenCaptureKit replaces ReplayKit for screen streaming and mirroring. A broadcast extension is no longer necessary.' The app presents the system SCContentSharingPicker. present() is used in Apple's sample for 'full-display capture' and presentForCurrentApplication() limits capture to the current app. That full-display capture includes other apps' content (Safari, Canvas) is a strong inference, not stated verbatim. Background modes table: 'Screen Capture | screen-capture | The app captures and streams screen content while in the background' (iOS, iPadOS, visionOS). Apple's iOS 27 sample: 'screen-capture in UIBackgroundModes, so the stream survives backgrounding for full-display capture' and 'audio, so the microphone tap keeps producing samples'. Before a full-display capture it activates an AVAudioSession in playAndRecord. The microphone is enabled by the user in the system picker: SCContentFilter.isMicrophoneEnabled is read-only and set via the picker's microphone control. SCStreamConfiguration.capturesAudio and SCStreamOutputType.audio exist on iPadOS 27.0+. Apple does not document that on iOS they capture other apps' audio (such as Safari video audio) in a full-display stream, and the Apple sample does not use them. That needs a device test. Apple's sample lists only NSCameraUsageDescription and NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription. No Apple page for an iOS NSScreenCaptureUsageDescription key was found (it returned 404), though third parties say it is required. Unverified developer reports say App Store Connect rejects 'screen-capture' as an invalid UIBackgroundModes value, which would block TestFlight distribution (see missed claims).

(b) The 'present() captures ... including other apps' wording is inferred from 'full-display'. The sample also notes that the camera preview's "underlying capture session pauses on backgrounding" (in-app mode only). Page platforms for the sample are iOS 27.0, iPadOS 27.0, Mac Catalyst 27.0 and Xcode 27.0.

claims.topic: Host and extension IPC: App Group and Darwin notifications
claims.final_claim: Darwin notifications are system-wide and carry only the name; object and userInfo are ignored. Data has to go through an App Group container or shared defaults. DTS says iOS does not resume a suspended app to deliver a Darwin notification: a suspended app gets it on resume, and a terminated app never gets it. For a system broadcast there is no documented host-side stop API. The host can only signal the extension (Darwin notification plus a flag in the App Group) and the extension calls finishBroadcastWithError(_:). broadcastFinished is documented as following the broadcasting app's finishBroadcast(handler:), which is the RPBroadcastController in-app flow.

claims.topic: Audio interruptions, mixing and iPad mic mute
claims.final_claim: An interruption deactivates our audio session. Interruptions happen when a competing audio session is activated that the system does not categorize as mixable with ours (archive guide, 2017-09-19). playAndRecord is nonmixable by default ('activating your session will interrupt any other audio sessions which are also nonmixable'), and mixWithOthers changes that. mixWithOthers can be set only for playAndRecord, playback and multiRoute, not record. The record category instead 'silences virtually all output on the system'. Documented: 'There is no guarantee that a begin interruption will have a corresponding end interruption.' InterruptionReason includes default, builtInMicMuted, routeDisconnected and sceneWasBackgrounded (appWasSuspended is deprecated). Closing an iPad Smart Folio mutes the built-in mic in hardware and interrupts the input session. overrideMutedMicrophoneInterruption (iPadOS 14.5+, playAndRecord only) keeps the session alive but delivers zero-valued samples. Route changes arrive through routeChangeNotification. interruptionNotification is iOS/iPadOS 6.0+, not deprecated on iOS/iPadOS, and deprecated on visionOS 27.0.
claims.verifier_note: The original said 'playAndRecord and record are nonmixable by default ... mixWithOthers changes that'. mixWithOthers cannot be applied to record, and record silences other output. The substance is otherwise verbatim. The 'no guarantee' sentence is only in the 2017 archive guide; the current 'Handling audio interruptions' page does not repeat it. The researcher's statement that Safari/Canvas playback will not interrupt a mixable session of ours is correctly flagged as needing a device test. Also documented in the interruptionNotification note: suspending the app deactivates its session, and the notification is delivered late with AVAudioSessionInterruptionWasSuspendedKey.

claims.topic: Live Activities as a session indicator on iPad
claims.final_claim: ActivityKit is available on iPadOS 16.1+, and Live Activities came to the iPad Lock Screen with iPadOS 17 (Apple Newsroom, 2023-06-05). A Live Activity can be active for up to 8 hours and remains on the Lock Screen for at most 12 hours. 'In general, your app needs to be in the foreground to start a Live Activity', but it can be started from the background through an App Intent conforming to LiveActivityIntent, and updated or ended from the background. Data is limited to 4 KB combined. iPads have no Dynamic Island. Per Apple: 'On an unlocked device that doesn't support the Dynamic Island, the Lock Screen presentation appears as a banner for Live Activity updates that include an alert configuration.' So while the user is in Safari on an unlocked iPad, a Live Activity is not a persistently visible session indicator. It shows only as transient banners on alerting updates.

claims.topic: Networking while suspended: WebSocket vs background URLSession
claims.final_claim: A running app's connections are not torn down, but a suspended app's sockets may be reclaimed and then fail. WebSocket tasks are not supported in background URLSessions; only delegate-based upload-from-file and download tasks are. Background sessions do the transfer in a separate system process and continue while the app is suspended or terminated by the system, but not after a user force-quit. Background sessions ignore waitsForConnectivity and always wait for connectivity. A connection that drops returns an error such as NSURLErrorNetworkConnectionLost.

device_tests_proposed: T1 (iPadOS 27, target iPad, TestFlight build, launched from the Home Screen, not under the Xcode debugger since DTS notes the debugger prevents suspension): start full-display ScreenCaptureKit (screen-capture and audio modes, active playAndRecord + mixWithOthers), then switch to Safari and play a bCourses video for 15 minutes. Expect video and audio sample timestamps to keep flowing and the WebSocket heartbeat to continue. Compare against the third-party report that capture froze on backgrounding.

T2: during ScreenCaptureKit capture, lock the screen for 2 minutes and unlock. Record whether stream(_:didStopWithError:) fires and with which code, whether frames resume, and whether mic samples continue while locked.

T4: force-quit the main app during ScreenCaptureKit capture. Expect the capture indicator to disappear right away (in-process). Log whether applicationWillTerminate or sceneDidDisconnect fired (not guaranteed). Relaunch and confirm the session shows as interrupted and the server marked it on heartbeat timeout.

T5 (fallback, iPadOS 26 and 27): start a ReplayKit broadcast, then force-quit the host app. Observe whether the red indicator stays, whether the extension keeps uploading (server-side frame counter), and whether broadcastFinished is called. Repeat with screen lock and an incoming FaceTime call.
T6 (fallback): broadcast at full iPad resolution for 30 minutes and measure extension memory in Instruments. Record any EXC_RESOURCE or jetsam limit to confirm or refute the 50 MB figure.

T7 (audio): with our mic running in the background (mixWithOthers), play and pause video in Safari and in Canvas Student, invoke Siri, and receive a call. Record every interruption began/ended notification with its reason and shouldResume, and whether the course video was paused when our session activated. Then try restarting the mic while backgrounded and check for cannotStartRecording.
T8: close the Smart Folio or Magic Keyboard cover during recording. Expect an interruption with reason builtInMicMuted. Verify how the app recovers after the cover is reopened.

T9: put our app in a window or Split View beside Safari with no background modes enabled. Log UIScene.activationState and whether timers and the WebSocket keep running while the user interacts only with Safari for 10 minutes.

T10: tap End, start BGContinuedProcessingTask plus a background URLSession upload of a 200 MB file, then go to the Home Screen. Expect a Live Activity with progress and the upload to finish. Repeat but force-quit mid-upload: expect it cancelled (NSURLErrorCancelled, force-quit reason) and resumable only after a manual relaunch.

T12: schedule a Time Sensitive break notification with a Focus mode on. Expect it to break through if the user allows it. Verify it fires while the app is suspended.
